Selection seed 20261119, exact panel, schedule, three repeats, whole-request bootstrap and endpoints were fixed before generation. No 0.5% success threshold, outlier removal, favorable-repeat selection or extra panel is applied. Report all completed measurements.

These measurements establish comparative serving behavior for fixed trained endpoints under this protocol. Distinct own-feedback histories and complete recipes do not isolate C allocation, a cap, or an AdaFlash loss term as the causal source. No seed-robustness or training-inclusive-speedup inference.

Checkpoints and input panel precede scoring, so serving outcomes did not choose these weights or requests. Temporal ordering does not identify why a training component helped; no learning-mechanism causal claim follows.

counter_definitions.native_accepted_draft_tokens: For each native verification:commit_rows−1; aggregate=sum across calls. Native average accepted length=sum(native_accepted)/sum(calls).
counter_definitions.accepted_draft_tokens: Stop-clipped matching trace counter:min(accepted_end−1,commit_rows), where accepted_end is the first mismatching proposal slot or block width16. It may exceed the native counter by one at a stop-clipped verification. It is not raw_accepted_draft_tokens_before_stop.
counter_definitions.committed_progress: Sum(commit_rows)=output_tokens−1 per request; the initial prefill-produced output token is excluded. Pooled progress/call=native accepted/call+1.
counter_definitions.raw_accepted_draft_tokens_before_stop: accepted_end−1; distinct from both retained summary counters. No substitution or reconstruction of stop-clipped counts from length alone.

limitations: One fixed seed17 training trajectory per recipe; no independent training or seed replication.
Freshness depends on the sealed historical-exclusion coverage, not on this numeric reducer.
Bootstrap intervals are marginal 95% intervals conditional on these fixed fitted endpoints.
Primary complete-request time contrast is C/released AdaFlash loss; secondary intervals are descriptive and unadjusted.
The comparison is fixed-model transfer within mathematics, not a new task-family result.
Complete recipes have distinct own-feedback histories; no isolated allocation or cap causal effect follows.
Native and stop-clipped acceptance are separate definitions.
Identical-output call and native-acceptance changes are coupled accounting views.
An interval spanning zero establishes neither equivalence nor nondegradation.
No minimum gain, automatic followup, tuning, enlarged panel or extra repeat is authorized.
Serving results exclude adaptation cost and do not establish training-inclusive speedup.
additional_limits: The paired request bootstrap is conditional on these fitted checkpoints and recorded timing measurements; it does not quantify training-seed variability or all shared-server timing uncertainty.
Freshness excludes known project uses/reservations under authenticated exposure coverage; unknown histories, semantic near duplicates and model pretraining are outside the claim.
No fourth KPLUS58 arm was measured here; do not combine historical KPLUS timing with this fresh panel.
A serving result for literal AREPO loss under the qualified fixed-length framework is not a reproduction or comparison of AdaFlash's entire high-concurrency system.

wording_review.supported: On this prespecified fresh MathQA panel, fixed C58 has lower complete-request time and fewer verification calls than fixed AREPO58, with positive paired95%lower bounds.
not_supported: C is training-seed robust or works across unrelated task families.
This is a training-inclusive speedup or full-system AdaFlash superiority.
Nonsignificance would prove equivalence or nondegradation.

repeat_cache_observation: Repeat 3 total cache-maintenance time increases for all three arms; all repeats and complete-request latencies remain included. Native-generation and cache timers are separate measured components; no detailed kernel explanation is inferred.
